newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rally to new highs in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rally to new highs in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks advanced strongly to new highs at the start of trading on Thursday, following through on gains on Wall Street and optimism on the economic outlook, brokers said.
"So where's the bad news?" Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities, asked rhetorically.
The Hang Seng Index shot up more than 100 points at the open to an all-time hihg of 12,880.78, before easing to trade 60 points up at 12,836.26 after 30 minutes of trade.
Turnover was a hefty HK$2.20 billion.

The Dow Industrials rose 96.53 points overnight to set a record close of 6,177.71, prompted by the re-election of a Democratic president and a Republican congress and the outlook for continued stability in U.S. economic policy and interest rates.
The Hang Seng Index set a new closing high on Wednesday of 12,775.47, as local and overseas investors took confidence in the U.S. election results.
"The market will be up quite strongly today, but in the end what counts is how strongly the U.S. economy is growing," said Claire Burges-Watson in institutional sales at Kim Eng Securities.
Burges-Watson pointed to the U.S. bond market's dip overnight and sluggishness in Tokyo early this morning as indications the outlook may be more balanced rather than bullish.
The U.S. long bond ended lower in New York trading on Wednesday, easing 14/32 to 6.62 percent, retracing almost half the advance of Tuesday.
"The market's previous consolidation was in the range of 12,200 to 12,600, so we can expect a measured move to 13,000," said Ted Chen, technical analyst at Technical Data Inc.
Chen's time frame for the move is end-November.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market, followed by properties. Mid cap issues were also sought,but H shares and the utilities sector lagged the market.
Banking giant HSBC Holding was the most active issue, putting on HK$1.50 to HK164.50, a new high for the stock.
Hutchison Whampoa was the second most active, rising HK$1.25 to HK$57.25. Brokers said they expect Hutchison to be one of the leaders in this rally.
Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.25 to HK$65.25, a new high, but Hongkong Telecom dipped HK$0.15 to HK$13.30.
